# Flow IR関連定義の自動抽出一覧

<!-- Generated by crates/emela-codegen-emb/tools/flow-ir-inventory.sh; schema_version=1. Do not edit. -->

Rustの構文解析から抽出した宣言・variant・field・属性・原文コメントの一覧。Flow/Heapの共有定義と、下記で指定したCoreの共有型を含む。**Flowへの出現可否、backendの対応、動作の正しさは未判定。** コメントは定義元の記述であり、組み込みtarget固有の契約への読み替えは行わない。

機械処理用: [flow-ir-inventory.json](flow-ir-inventory.json)。安定IDと宣言のSHA-256で実装側の記録を照合できる。件数は機能数や試験数を表さない。

抽出結果: 428件（variant 195件、field 190件、型宣言・alias 43件）。

## emela_lir::Suspend

| ID | 種別 | 宣言 | 原文コメント | 属性 | 定義 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>emela_lir::Suspend</code> | struct | <code>struct Suspend</code> | The suspension edge of a value in a suspending function (Heap IR, from<br>`Stage::StateMachines`): a resume point of the function's state machine.<br><br>The value (a suspending call, a waiting concurrency operation or a fairness yield) either comes<br>back as usual (fast path: nothing is allocated, the variables stay in locals), or comes back<br>suspended. Then a frame of the function is allocated with `state` and the `saved` variables<br>(moved into it), pushed onto the continuation being captured, and the function returns<br>(suspended) to its caller, which does the same up to the runtime's driver loop. When the<br>runtime resumes the frame, the function is entered again with the frame: the saved variables<br>are restored and control continues right after the value as if it had come back with the<br>resumed input (its value in `dst`, or a pending failure or defect for the landings). | <code># [derive (Debug , Clone , PartialEq , Eq)]</code> | [L311](../../../emela-lir/src/ir.rs#L311) |
| <code>emela_lir::Suspend.state</code> | field | <code>pub state : u32</code> | The resume point, unique in the function (numbered from 0). | <code></code> | [L324](../../../emela-lir/src/ir.rs#L324) |
| <code>emela_lir::Suspend.saved</code> | field | <code>pub saved : Vec &lt; VarId &gt;</code> | The variables saved in the frame, in slot order: every variable live after the value (on<br>any way on, the landings included) and the references the value borrows, so that the<br>resumed function owns exactly what the uninterrupted one owns after the value. | <code></code> | [L326](../../../emela-lir/src/ir.rs#L326) |

## emela_core::OpDef

| ID | 種別 | 宣言 | 原文コメント | 属性 | 定義 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>emela_core::OpDef</code> | struct | <code>struct OpDef</code> | An effect operation (spec 8.1), with its types for the instantiation of its effect.<br><br>An operation may have type parameters of its own only in built-in effects (`fork[A]` and<br>`deferred[A]` of Scope, spec 8.1, 11.2). They are `Type::Param(0..type_params)` in `params` and<br>`ret`, instantiated per call by `Callee::Op::ty_args`. The type arguments of built-in effects<br>are sets (`Scope[E, R]`), so such an operation's types contain no other `Type::Param`. A<br>handler implements a generic operation for every instantiation at once, so its implementation<br>sees the operation's own type parameters as `Type::Any`.<br><br>Why type parameters rather than `Any` in the `OpDef` itself: so that the value of a call<br>(`Fiber[Int]` from `s.fork[Int](..)`) has a type the IR alone determines. The type checker<br>records the instantiation at the operation reference, so filling `Callee::Op::ty_args` costs<br>no more than for a direct call. | <code># [derive (Debug , Clone , PartialEq , Eq)]</code> | [L457](../../../emela-core/src/ir.rs#L457) |
